title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE'
what_happened: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders the First Light detection as 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed - possible new transient / 13h 29m 52s +47 11' 43" / mag 2.4 [NAKED EYE]'. The detection row has delta_mag = -2.35 (a brightness CHANGE in magnitudes relative to the atlas template) and no photometric zero point anywhere in the pipeline -- there is no apparent magnitude for this object at all. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets `magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs()`, and the card at transient_card.dart:581 then buckets `magnitude <= 6.0` as NAKED EYE, <= 10 BINOCULAR, <= 14 SMALL SCOPE. Because a difference-image delta magnitude of more than ~6 is essentially impossible, EVERY First Light self-discovery that has a measured delta is announced as a naked-eye or binocular object. The app is telling the user they have found a magnitude-2.4 supernova -- brighter than Polaris, and the brightest supernova in recorded history.
expected: Do not populate the alert's apparent-magnitude field from a delta magnitude. Either leave magnitude null (the card already handles a null magnitude by omitting the chip) and show the delta separately as 'Δ2.35 mag', or compute a real apparent magnitude from a photometric zero point when one exists. The NAKED EYE / BINOCULAR / SMALL SCOPE bucketing must never run on a delta.
repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='newSource', delta_mag=-2.35, snr=18.4, reviewed=1. 2. Restart the app. 3. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 4. Read the chip on the alert card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png: green chip 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE' next to a card titled 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova'. DB: select id,kind,delta_mag,snr,fwhm from transient_detections -> 1|newSource|-2.35|18.4|2.41. There is no apparent-magnitude column on the table at all and photometric_transforms is empty, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction.
proposed_fix: Add a distinct deltaMag field to TransientAlert and leave `magnitude` null for First Light detections; render 'Δ 2.35 mag brighter' instead of 'mag 2.4', and suppress the brightness bucket entirely when only a delta is known.
verdict_reasoning: Code, data and UI all check out. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 is exactly 'final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();' and is passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude, the apparent-magnitude field every alert surface consumes. transient_card.dart:580-588 _getBrightnessInfo buckets magnitude<=6 NAKED EYE / <=10 BINOCULAR / <=14 SMALL SCOPE, called at :532 and rendered as 'mag ${magnitude.toStringAsFixed(1)}' at :553. DB: transient_detections has exactly one row, kind=newSource delta_mag=-2.35 snr=18.4, and the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction. Confirmed live on my own profile: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed — possible new transient / mag 2.4 / NAKED EYE'. Because a difference-image delta larger than ~6 mag is essentially impossible, every First Light self-discovery with a measured delta is bucketed NAKED EYE or BINOCULAR. Cited file:line is precise.

title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
what_happened: The improvement curve is derived from the master that was just produced. Because that master contained only 1 registered frame (see the P0 above), the persisted curve has one point and a recommendation of {keepN: 1, predictedSnrGainPct: 0.0, reason: 'Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)'}. The cull rail then renders an enabled primary action 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' whose tooltip is 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best 1 subs (+0% SNR)'. Pressing it three times changed nothing (still 9 accepted in the DB) and toasted 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. So the control knows the curve does not match the 9 accepted subs, yet still renders a specific, quantified, actionable label -- and its remedy is to re-run the same integration that produced the stale curve.
expected: The rail must decide staleness at render time, not at press time. When the curve's population does not cover the currently-accepted subs, or when predictedSnrGainPct <= 0, show a disabled/absent action (or an explicit 'analysis out of date' chip) rather than a confident 'Keep best 1 (+0%)'. A control should not offer an operation it will unconditionally refuse.
repro: 1. Do the Integrate-now repro above (produces a 1-frame master). 2. A new button 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' appears beside Blink mode / Select-lasso. 3. Click it. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db "select count(*) from captured_images where session_id=1 and is_accepted=1" -> still 9; toast reads 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png, rsr-22.png, rsr-25.png show 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' while the header reads '9 accepted - 1 rejected'; AT-SPI tree after the click contains 'panel: Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. DB improvement_curve_json for master 2: {"points":[{"n":1,...}],"recommendation":{"keepN":1,"keptIndices":[0],"predictedSnrGainPct":0.0,"reason":"Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)"},"population":[".../audit_L_001.fits"]} -- population length 1 vs 9 accepted, which is exactly the staleCurve guard in session_review_controller.dart:1377.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/widgets/sub_cull_rail.dart:473 (tooltip) and :475 (label 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct}%)'); guard in session_review_controller.dart:1354 cullToRecommended()
location_wrong: cullToRecommended() is at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1418-1480 in the rebuilt tree, not :1354 (the file grew 66 lines in the fix wave); sub_cull_rail.dart:473/475 are exact.
proposed_fix: Lift the population-vs-accepted comparison out of cullToRecommended() into a getter the rail reads while building, and gate the button on it plus predictedSnrGainPct > 0.
verdict_reasoning: The render-time/press-time asymmetry is exactly what the current source does, and the two cited widget lines are exact. sub_cull_rail.dart:274 passes the action through whenever `curve != null && curve.recommendation.keepN > 0` -- no population check, no gain check -- and :470-480 renders an enabled primary SkotiqButton labelled 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct.toStringAsFixed(0)}%)' (:475) inside a Tooltip 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best $keepN subs (+…% SNR)' (:473). Every staleness test lives in the press handler instead: SessionReviewController.cullToRecommended() returns CullToRecommendedResult.staleCurve when the curve's population length differs from the accepted set, when paths duplicate, or when any population path is no longer accepted, and alreadyOptimal when keepN >= population.length. So in those states the control can only ever be pressed to be refused while still advertising a specific quantified action. This is NOT contingent on the P0 that produced the 1-frame master: any accept/reject after an integration diverges the population, and the alreadyOptimal case renders a '+0%' button that also refuses. Not re-driven live (needs a session with real FITS subs, which the scratch profile has none of); the source is unambiguous.

title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead on a default install, and only the currently-selected network's blocker is explained
what_happened: Submit discovery opens with Network = TNS and an amber line 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name, reporting group, data source, reporter, and api key -- configure them in Settings > Science.' Clicking the AAVSO chip does nothing (verified twice, once with coordinates measured from a cropped region shot so the hit point was unambiguous); TNS stays selected. Preview and 'Submit to TNS' are equally inert -- no dialog, no snackbar, no log line, no file. All three chips are disabled because _formatEnabled is false for each: AAVSO needs an observer code AND a magnitude zero point, MPC needs an observatory code AND a mover-class detection, TNS needs the five bot fields. None of the chips render a disabled affordance, and the panel prints a reason only for the format that happens to be selected, so a user who wants the AAVSO export -- the cheapest one to enable, it needs a single settings field -- gets a chip that silently ignores them and a message about TNS credentials that has nothing to do with their problem.
expected: A disabled chip must look disabled and must say why on hover/press. Better: list all three networks with their individual status ('AAVSO - needs observer code', 'MPC - not a moving object', 'TNS - needs bot key') so the user can see at a glance which one is reachable and what it costs.
repro: 1. Seed a confirmed newSource detection. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Submit. 3. Click AAVSO -> nothing; TNS stays selected (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-19.png vs rsr2-20.png are identical). 4. Click Preview -> nothing, no snackbar within 1s, nothing in the log.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-18.png (whole dialog), rsr2-19.png and rsr2-20.png (network row before and after an AAVSO click, byte-for-byte the same state). Source: transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 (`onTap: enabled ? ... : null`) and :142-148 (the reason block only renders _disabledReason for `_format`).
proposed_fix: Render disabled chips at reduced opacity with a tooltip carrying that format's own _disabledReason, and show a per-format status list instead of a single reason line.
verdict_reasoning: Verified in source at the cited lines and reproduced live. transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 renders the three chips with `onTap: enabled ? ... : null`, and :142-151 renders _disabledReason ONLY for the selected `_format`. _formatEnabled at :343-367 gates every format on d.reviewed, then aavso on aavsoAvailable + non-empty settings.aavsoObserverCode, mpc on a non-empty mpcObservatoryCode + a plausible-mover kind, tns on complete bot creds -- all false on a default install. skotiq_chip.dart:65-68 returns the bare chip when onTap is null: same fill, border and text colour as an enabled unselected chip, no Semantics, no cursor change, so a disabled chip is indistinguishable and silently swallows the tap. Preview/Copy at :296-320 are gated the same way. LIVE (profile v2-science-review, display :86): seeded one newSource detection, confirmed it (DB reviewed=1), First Light > Submit opens on TNS with the amber 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name...' line; clicking AAVSO changes nothing -- TNS stays selected and the TNS-specific reason stays on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png before, v2sr-13.png after).
